title: HPE Surges 29 Per Cent. Marvell Is Called the Next Trillion-Dollar Company. Micron Crosses $1,000. The AI Spending Boom Just Entered a New Phase.
excerpt: In 24 hours, four companies made the same point: AI infrastructure spending is accelerating faster than anyone predicted. Here is what NRI investors need to know about the week ahead.
body:
In a single 24-hour window, four separate pieces of news have made the same point with escalating force: the artificial intelligence infrastructure buildout is accelerating faster than almost anyone predicted, and the companies supplying the picks and shovels are being repriced in real time.

Hewlett Packard Enterprise surged as much as 29 per cent in premarket trading after reporting record second-quarter results that blew past every estimate on Wall Street. Marvell Technology jumped 21 per cent after Nvidia's Jensen Huang called it the "next trillion-dollar company" at the Computex conference in Taipei. Micron Technology closed above $1,000 for the first time, entering the trillion-dollar market capitalisation club. And Alphabet announced plans to raise $80 billion in equity offerings — including an investment from Berkshire Hathaway — to fund AI infrastructure expansion.

The S&P 500 and the Nasdaq have now logged eight consecutive sessions of gains and closed at record highs. The S&P 500 is up nine weeks in a row, a streak last witnessed in late 2023.

## HPE: The Numbers That Stunned Wall Street

HPE reported quarterly revenue of $10.7 billion, up 40 per cent year-over-year and well ahead of the $9.8 billion Wall Street expected. Adjusted earnings came in at $0.79 per share — beating consensus of $0.54 by 46 per cent. The company's Cloud and AI segment generated $7.7 billion in revenue, with server revenue alone hitting $5.5 billion, up 33 per cent.

Orders more than doubled and the company entered the quarter with a record backlog. AI systems bookings reached $1.8 billion in the quarter, bringing cumulative AI bookings to $16.4 billion and the AI backlog to $5.9 billion.

Most strikingly, HPE pulled forward its long-term financial targets by two years. The company now expects fiscal 2026 revenue growth of 29 to 33 per cent, up from its prior guidance of 17 to 22 per cent. It also guided for fiscal 2027 revenue growth of 8 to 12 per cent — figures that would have been considered ambitious a quarter ago.

"This is probably one of the most critical inflection points that we've ever seen," said an analyst at Raymond James.

## Marvell and the Trillion-Dollar Endorsement

At Computex in Taipei, Jensen Huang — whose endorsements have become the most consequential in the semiconductor industry — called Marvell Technology the "next trillion-dollar company." Nvidia invested $2 billion in Marvell in March, and the chipmaker's shares responded immediately with a 21 per cent surge.

Marvell designs custom silicon and networking chips that are critical to AI data centres. As hyperscalers like Google, Amazon, and Microsoft build out custom AI accelerators alongside Nvidia GPUs, Marvell's role as the connective tissue of the AI data centre has become increasingly clear to investors.

## Micron Crosses $1,000

Micron Technology closed at $1,034.74 on Monday, its first close above $1,000. The memory-chip maker's market capitalisation has crossed $1 trillion, driven by insatiable demand for high-bandwidth memory chips that power AI training and inference.

The company is run by Indian-American CEO Sanjay Mehrotra, who co-founded SanDisk and has led Micron's transformation into an AI infrastructure powerhouse. Raymond James raised its price target to $1,100, while D.A. Davidson went to $1,500, arguing that Micron, SK Hynix, and Samsung own "almost the entire" DRAM and high-bandwidth memory market with no meaningful competition on the horizon.

Micron's revenue trajectory tells the story: $13.6 billion two quarters ago, $23.9 billion last quarter, and guidance for $33.5 billion next quarter — a 263 per cent year-over-year growth rate. The stock is up 240 per cent year to date and more than 900 per cent over the past year.

## Alphabet's $80 Billion Raise

Alphabet announced plans to raise $80 billion through equity offerings, including a strategic investment from Berkshire Hathaway, to fund the expansion of its AI infrastructure. The move underscores the sheer scale of capital required to compete in the AI race. Alphabet shares slipped nearly 2 per cent on the dilution, but the signal was clear: Google is willing to raise unprecedented capital to maintain its position.

## What NRI Tech Investors Should Know

For diaspora investors with exposure to the US tech sector — whether through individual stocks, index funds, or retirement accounts — the message is that the AI infrastructure cycle is not slowing down. If anything, HPE's pulled-forward guidance and Micron's parabolic revenue growth suggest it is accelerating.

But the risk profile is also changing. Money markets have all but priced out rate cuts for 2026 and see growing odds of an eventual rate hike, driven by inflationary pressures from the Iran conflict and energy prices. Brent crude is trading around $94 a barrel. A prolonged war could push inflation higher and force the Federal Reserve into tighter policy — the one thing that could derail the AI rally.

The week ahead brings the JOLTS job openings report on Tuesday, Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack's comments later in the day, and Friday's pivotal employment report. Broadcom reports earnings on Wednesday. Each data point will test whether this rally has legs — or whether the market is pricing perfection into an imperfect world.
author: Diaspora Desk
